Follow INSTALL.md in https://github.com/solwation/dirigenten-och-orkestern: the latest release as a git subtree under .orchestra/shared, a project policy in .orchestra/project.md based on PROJECT.example.md, the /orkester command for Claude (.claude/commands/orkester.md) and the Codex skill (.agents/skills/orkester/SKILL.md), linked from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. close.title: Close all
close.confirm: Active AI turns will be interrupted. Each AI then continues the latest conversation in its directory to save, commit and push completed work. Tabs close after that turn. Permissions can prevent saving. Shells and finished one-shot runs close immediately. Agents without safe conversation resumption need manual saving. Continue?

close.saveFailed: The save turn failed or was denied. Check the terminal before forcing it closed.

compact.title: Auto-compact
compact.source.claude: Official native context window. Confirm or change for a gateway or restricted context mode.
compact.source.codex: Local Codex model metadata, including effective context percentage. Confirm for custom provider/context settings.
compact.source.manual: Unknown or custom capacity: enter a verified token count from your model/provider. No capacity is guessed.
compact.unit.claude: Automatic compaction window: 100,000–1,000,000 tokens. The CLI reserves space before the limit. Support is checked at startup. CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW takes precedence.
compact.unit.codex: Token budget for automatic history compaction, counting the entire active context. Does not change the context window or separate post-turn compaction.
compact.unit.aider: Soft token budget for chat history ONLY. The recommendation additionally reserves half the context for code, map and instructions; adapt it to the project size.
compact.unit.unsupported: No verified equivalent setting in this CLI. Configure any compaction in the agent itself.
compact.model.required: Choose an exact model ID. The CLI default model can change and receives no assumed capacity.
compact.unknown: No recommendation: capacity is unknown or too small for the profile reserve and CLI limits. Use CLI default or a valid custom value.
compact.recommendation: Suggestion: {0} tokens = capacity {1} − turn/tool reserve {2} − file budget {3}, rounded down to thousands.
compact.tradeoff: Heuristic: questions reserve 10% (at least 16k), code 25% (32k), orchestra 40% (64k). Lower limits leave more room but cause more summaries and lose detail. Applies to new or explicitly restarted matching tabs. Auto-clear is separate and empties history.
compact.saved: Saved. Running sessions continue; restart when you want to apply this choice.
agents.intro: CLI version is the program version. Choose models per project; an installed CLI does not identify a model version.
agents.mode.title: Alias / permissions
agents.mode.standard.detail: Starts the CLI without extra permission flags from an alias. The CLI’s own settings and organization policies decide when it asks; they are not reset.
agents.mode.custom.detail: Your custom shell definition controls startup. Choose a preset to compare its effect and apply it after confirmation.
agents.mode.unsupported: This mode is not supported by the detected CLI. Check versions again.
agents.mode.claude.auto: Automatically accepts edits and common filesystem commands in working directories (acceptEdits). Other tools may still ask. Does not change sandbox configuration.
agents.mode.claude.yolo: Skips the agent’s permission prompts. Organization policies and some safeguards still apply. Does not create an isolated environment.
agents.mode.codex.auto: Uses automatic approval review while retaining the workspace-write sandbox. Risky or denied actions can still be stopped.
agents.mode.codex.yolo: Disables approval prompts and the CLI sandbox. The agent receives the permissions of the user and its surrounding environment.
agents.mode.agy.auto: Auto mode approves edits and safe commands with terminal sandboxing. Requires a supported environment and account; the CLI may fall back to default when unavailable.
agents.mode.agy.yolo: Approves every tool request without asking. This alias does not create a sandbox; the agent’s separate sandbox setting still applies.
agents.mode.aider.yolo: Answers yes to every confirmation. Adds no isolation; tools and file edits use the environment’s existing permissions.
agents.mode.openhands.auto: Uses the agent’s LLM-based security analyzer for approvals. Does not change the selected local, container, or cloud environment.
agents.mode.openhands.yolo: Approves all actions without questions. Keeps the selected execution environment but adds no isolation.
agents.mode.interpreter.auto: No manual approval prompts, while retaining the workspace-write sandbox. Actions outside the allowed boundary are denied. Applies to the current standalone CLI.
agents.mode.interpreter.legacyYolo: Legacy Python CLI: runs generated code automatically without confirmation. Adds no sandbox.
agents.applies: Changes apply to new tabs and restarts where BoosterAI owns the alias. Running turns and custom aliases are preserved. Older tabs may need closing and reopening.
agents.mode.applied: {0}: {1} saved. Applies to new tabs and restarts where BoosterAI owns the alias.
agents.yolo.title: Enable YOLO for {0}?
agents.yolo.code: Alias saved in the BoosterAI block in ~/.bashrc:
agents.yolo.warning: YOLO removes the agent’s normal approval prompts and may also disable its sandbox. The agent can change or delete files and execute commands without asking. Read this agent’s specific effect below. This also affects new regular terminals that read your alias block.
agents.description.claude: Claude Code – coding and tools from Anthropic.
agents.description.codex: Codex – OpenAI’s agent for coding and project work.
agents.description.aider: Aider – code changes with hosted or local models.
agents.description.interpreter: Open Interpreter – local code execution and agent work.
agents.description.openhands: OpenHands CLI – agent for development tasks.
agents.update.claude: Update uses the official installer. Automatic CLI updates can also check before launch.
agents.update.codex: Installed and updated with npm in the tab’s environment. Requires Node.js/npm.
agents.update.agy: Update uses the official installer in the tab’s environment.
agents.update.aider: Update uses Aider’s official installer. Configure local models separately.
agents.update.interpreter: Installs the current standalone version. Legacy Python installations are not migrated automatically; modes follow detected flags.
agents.update.openhands: Installs OpenHands CLI. Configure its LLM and local/container environment in the agent.
compact.unit.interpreter: Current Open Interpreter: token budget for automatic history compaction, through a per-run -c override. Legacy Python CLI is unsupported. Confirm the local model’s context capacity.
compact.custom.invalid: Enter a whole token count: Claude 100,000–1,000,000, others 1–10,000,000 (app safety bound), at most the specified capacity. Choose an exact model ID.
agents.mode.editHint: Choose a mode and Apply to save the agent alias. YOLO requires an additional confirmation.
agents.compact.editHint: Manual history-budget tuning. Choose the global mode under Optimization → Auto-compact.
compact.global.title: Auto-compact for all tabs
compact.global.intro: Choose how BoosterAI sets the automatic history-compaction budget.
compact.global.off.detail: The CLI’s own defaults apply, including its automatic compaction.
compact.global.auto.detail: Auto calculates a threshold when capacity is known. Otherwise, CLI defaults apply.
compact.global.manual.detail: Your saved model choices apply. Fine-tune them under AI agents.
compact.global.modes: Off: no budget overrides. Auto: a calculated budget when capacity is available. Manual: your saved model choices.
compact.global.auto.profile: Orchestra tabs use Long orchestra run: a 40% reserve, at least 64,000 tokens. Other tabs use Code changes: 25%, at least 32,000. The remainder is rounded down to thousands. The reserve leaves room for the next turn and tool results; more compaction can cost time and detail.
compact.global.metadata.ready: Codex model metadata is available. Only exact model IDs with a known capacity receive an automatic budget.
compact.global.metadata.missing: Codex capacity is not known yet: CLI defaults apply until model metadata has been read. No budget is guessed.
compact.global.auto.fallback: Claude uses documented native context for known model IDs. Gateways, custom providers or restricted context modes may require verified capacity in Manual. Default models, unknown/local models and other agents without verified capacity retain CLI defaults. Auto is a heuristic, not a guarantee of optimal efficiency.
compact.global.advanced: Open AI agents for manual tuning
compact.global.applies: Applies to new and explicitly restarted sessions. Running work is not interrupted. Saved manual choices remain in every mode. Auto-clear is separate and empties history.
compact.edit.manual: Manual is selected in Optimization. These changes affect only this agent’s compaction settings.
compact.edit.locked: Select Manual under Optimization → Auto-compact to edit, save or reset. Your saved values and drafts are preserved.
compact.reset.detail: Clears only this agent’s compaction choices for all models and profiles, plus its unsaved draft. Permissions and other agents are unchanged.
compact.reset.done: This agent’s compaction choices are reset to CLI defaults.

agents.alias.what: An alias is a shell shortcut: for example, codex can automatically expand to codex with extra permission flags. It also affects ordinary terminals that read the same shell settings.
agents.alias.unverified.detail: The CLI is unavailable or detection has not completed. Check installation and versions first.
agents.alias.function.detail: The custom shell function can add flags or run multiple commands. Choose a preset to replace its startup behavior after confirmation.
agents.alias.external.detail: This is your custom alias. A selected preset can replace it after confirmation. Other aliases and CLI settings stay unchanged.
agents.alias.managed.detail: This alias is active in the checked shell and managed in the BoosterAI block in ~/.bashrc.
agents.alias.none.detail: No alias or shell function is active for this name. The CLI’s own permission settings apply.
agents.alias.block.detail: An unrecognized alias block was found. A selected preset can replace this agent’s startup definition after confirmation.
agents.alias.truncated: Only the beginning of the function is shown (at most 8 KiB).
agents.alias.recommend: Recommended starting point: No alias. Choose Auto Approve to automate more approvals; read this agent’s effect below.
agents.alias.remove: After confirmation, removes the BoosterAI permission alias. CLI settings stay unchanged.
agents.alias.write: After confirmation, writes this alias in the BoosterAI block in ~/.bashrc.
agents.alias.scope: Applies to new terminals and tabs reading the same shell settings, and explicit restarts in tabs supporting this preset. Running work is unchanged.
agents.alias.definitionMissing: The definition could not be read. You can still choose a preset and confirm its replacement.
agents.alias.recommend.basic: Recommended starting point: No alias. This keeps the CLI’s own settings. YOLO is an explicit choice to run without ordinary approval prompts.
agents.alias.preview.external: After confirmation this preset replaces the alias or function for this agent. Original definition lines are preserved.

shutdownWsl.body: All WSL distributions will stop, including those not used by BoosterAI. Terminals, AI sessions and background processes will end. Save your work first.
shutdownWsl.detail: This action does not save your work. WSL starts again on next use and reads the saved resource settings. Saving the memory limit alone does not shut down WSL.
project.remove.blocked: Close all tabs in this project first. An AI session or terminal shell is still open.

setup.title: Install BoosterAI
setup.welcome.heading: Welcome to BoosterAI
setup.welcome.body: BoosterAI opens your projects in work tabs with an AI CLI in each. This guide installs the app for your user, without administrator rights. Along the way you can choose a few settings and find your projects.
setup.welcome.skip: Every step except the installation itself can be skipped, and everything can be changed later in Settings.
setup.welcome.upgrade: BoosterAI is already installed. Installing replaces the program and keeps your projects and settings.
setup.settings.heading: Basic settings
setup.settings.body: Choose the language, appearance and the AI CLI your projects start with. Everything can be changed later in Settings.
setup.llm.title: AI CLI
setup.llm.name: AI CLI for new projects
setup.llm.hint: Starts in the projects you find in the next step.
setup.projects.heading: Find projects
setup.projects.body: Search for folders with git or AI instructions and choose which ones become projects in BoosterAI.
setup.projects.none: No projects chosen yet. You can also add projects later.
setup.install.heading: Ready to install
setup.install.body: This happens when you click Install:
setup.install.shortcuts: Shortcuts are created in the Start menu and on the desktop, and BoosterAI is added to Apps & features so it can be uninstalled.
setup.install.upgrade: A BoosterAI running from the install folder is closed first and replaced.
setup.install.settingsKept: The settings are left as they are.
setup.install.config: Existing projects and settings in {0} are kept.
setup.install.start: BoosterAI starts in the background when the installation is done.
setup.progress.shortcuts: Creating shortcuts and the Apps & features entry…
setup.error.locked: Could not replace {0} after {1} attempts (the file is in use by another process). Close BoosterAI and try again.
setup.error.start: BoosterAI exited right after the installation (code {0}). Start the program again.
setup.error.windowsOnly: The setup guide is for Windows only. Use install-linux.sh on Linux.
setup.done.heading: BoosterAI is installed
setup.done.body: BoosterAI runs in the background and is in the Start menu and on the desktop. Open the window to start your projects.
setup.done.otherRunning: Another BoosterAI was already running, so no extra instance was started. Restart it to use the newly installed version.
setup.shortcut.description: Start work tabs with an AI CLI
uninstall.heading: Uninstall BoosterAI?
uninstall.body: BoosterAI is closed and removed for your user on this computer.
uninstall.detail: Your projects and settings in {0} are kept, so a new installation continues where you left off.
localAdvice.title: Local model on this computer
localAdvice.selection: Selection when the advice window opened: {0} / {1}
localAdvice.intro: Advice for Aider, Open Interpreter and OpenHands. Check that the model and server below match the agent’s actual settings. These choices do not change CLI settings or prevent starting.
localAdvice.selection.Ollama: Ollama is selected, but its server location is unknown. CLI environment, saved settings or custom aliases may select another server. Confirm below to assess this computer.
localAdvice.selection.Api: The model name suggests API/remote inference. This computer’s RAM and GPU then do not determine model performance. CLI settings can change the server; only confirm below if you actually use a local Ollama model.
localAdvice.selection.Unknown: Insufficient information: the actual model, backend or execution location cannot be determined from the tab selection. Enter an exact installed Ollama model and confirm its server for local advice. Other backends need separate checking.
localAdvice.notMeasured: Hardware has not been read yet.
localAdvice.model: Exact Ollama model for assessment (including tag)
localAdvice.endpoint: Ollama address for assessment (loopback HTTP only)
localAdvice.confirm: I checked that the agent uses this server on the same operating system as BoosterAI, without WSL/container/remote inference.
localAdvice.cpuOnly: The server is configured for CPU inference without a GPU (optional, for advice before the model is loaded).
localAdvice.confirmRequired: Hardware has been read. Confirm the server location to compare it with a local model. Unknown or remote models receive no local hardware verdict.
localAdvice.invalidEndpoint: Enter a loopback HTTP address, for example http://127.0.0.1:11434. Proxies, redirects and remote addresses are not used.
localAdvice.exactModelRequired: Enter the exact Ollama model ID. standard or local does not identify a particular model.
localAdvice.checking: Reading installed and already loaded models…
localAdvice.failed: Model metadata could not be read. The server may be offline, require authentication or return an unknown format. No performance verdict is available. Nothing was downloaded or started.
localAdvice.cpu: CPU: {0} · {1} available logical processors (no speed test)
localAdvice.gpuUnknown: GPU/VRAM: unknown. The NVIDIA tool is unavailable or returned no reliable value. AMD/Intel are not read; this does not mean there is no GPU.
localAdvice.platform: RAM/CPU describe the environment running BoosterAI. Windows reports the host, not WSL’s allowed RAM. Linux reports its /proc environment; container limits can differ. GPU support and the server’s actual use must be checked separately.
localAdvice.metadata: Installed model: {0} · file size {1} (measured, not the full memory requirement)
localAdvice.runtimeUnknown: Loaded models could not be read; the CPU/GPU distribution is unknown.
localAdvice.verdict.Remote: The model runs on a remote server.
localAdvice.verdict.Limited: This local model will probably not perform well on your computer.
localAdvice.verdict.Fits: Memory capacity appears suitable for the current loaded configuration.
localAdvice.reason.missingModel: The exact model and tag were not found among installed models. No size is guessed from the name. No model is downloaded.
localAdvice.reason.remote: Ollama identifies a remote/cloud model, even though the server address is local. This computer’s RAM and VRAM therefore do not produce a warning about this model.
localAdvice.reason.gpuLoaded: Ollama reports that the same model version is already fully loaded on GPU. This shows current memory placement, not response speed or code quality. Larger context and concurrent requests can require more memory.
localAdvice.reason.splitLoaded: Ollama reports that the same model version is split across CPU and GPU. CPU work can make responses slow. Consider a smaller or remote model; speed has not been measured.
localAdvice.reason.cpuLoaded: Ollama reports that the same model version is loaded without GPU. CPU inference can be slow even with sufficient RAM. Consider a smaller or remote model; speed has not been measured.
localAdvice.reason.ramTotal: For confirmed CPU inference, the model file alone is at least as large as all measured RAM. Inference also needs context and working memory and may cause swapping or memory errors. Choose a smaller or remote model.
localAdvice.reason.ramAvailable: For confirmed CPU inference, RAM available now is no larger than the model file, before context and working memory. Close other programs or choose a smaller/remote model. Available RAM can change; this is a conservative file-size comparison.
localAdvice.reason.cpuUnloaded: CPU inference is confirmed but the model is not loaded. Quantization, context, runtime and CPU speed determine actual memory use and response time. CPU inference can be slow; consider a smaller or remote model.
localAdvice.reason.unloaded: The model is not loaded. File size cannot predict memory requirements or speed. GPU support, actual CPU/GPU distribution, quantization, context and concurrency remain unknown.
localAdvice.gpuSmall: Measured GPU {0}: {1} total VRAM, smaller than the model file’s {2}. If the server uses this GPU, CPU offload may be needed and responses may be slow. Other GPUs and the actual backend can change this.
localAdvice.limits: The check reads RAM/CPU, an optional NVIDIA query (at most 3 s) and Ollama’s /api/tags and /api/ps (bounded responses and deadline). No generation, download or benchmark runs. File size is a rough lower comparison, not a full requirement: quantization, context/KV cache, runtime and concurrency matter. Free VRAM is not summed across GPUs and does not prove compatibility. Readings and confirmations are not saved.
localAdvice.verdict.Caution: CPU inference may limit performance; response time has not been measured.
agents.status.unknown: Status has not been checked yet
agents.status.checking: Checking agent status in the background …
agents.status.failed: Agent status could not be checked. Opening this page later will retry automatically.
agents.status.failed.previous: The check failed. Showing the last known agent status. Opening this page later will retry automatically.
settingsAdvice.title: Local model on this computer
settingsAdvice.status.modelDependent: Local: choose a model for advice
settingsAdvice.status.cpuRoom: Example: model file fits in RAM
settingsAdvice.reason.pending: You can use the agent with cloud/API models without a powerful local GPU. Local inference needs a model and memory requirements. Hardware is read automatically when you open AI agents.
settingsAdvice.reason.checking: Reading RAM, CPU and available GPU information. No models are downloaded or started. You can still install the agent for cloud/API use.
settingsAdvice.reason.modelDependent: No local model is selected for assessment. We cannot recommend or advise against local inference yet. The agent can also use cloud/API models, where this computer’s GPU and RAM do not determine model performance.
settingsAdvice.reason.gpuUnknown: OpenHands specifies at least 24 GB VRAM for this quantized Qwen example. No reliable GPU capacity could be read here. This does not mean there is no GPU. Check the model server’s GPU support or use a remote model.
settingsAdvice.reason.gpuLevel: A measured GPU reaches OpenHands’ documented level of at least 24 GB VRAM for this Qwen example. This supports planning, not a guarantee of compatibility or speed. Context and concurrent requests may need more memory.
settingsAdvice.reason.gpuSmall: Measured VRAM per GPU is below OpenHands’ documented 24 GB level for this Qwen example. This local model will probably not perform well on your computer in the planned GPU configuration. Choose a smaller or remote model. Multi-GPU configurations need separate checking.
settingsAdvice.reason.ramUnknown: This example assumes CPU inference with a model file of about 4.7 GB, but RAM could not be read. Full memory requirements and response time are unknown. No recommendation is given without that information.
settingsAdvice.reason.cpuRamSmall: RAM available now is below the published model file size of about 4.7 GB, before context and working memory. This local model will probably not perform well on your computer for planned CPU inference. Close other programs, choose a smaller model or use a remote model.
settingsAdvice.reason.cpuRoom: Available RAM appears to fit the published model file of about 4.7 GB. Context and working memory are additional. CPU inference may be slow; this is not a speed measurement or a recommendation of the model’s coding quality.
settingsAdvice.next.choose: Next: compare a named example below, or use the agent with cloud/API models. Your choice does not change CLI settings.
settingsAdvice.next.model: This advice applies only to the model and assumptions here, not the agent or cloud/API use. You can still install. Check model server support and actual context before local inference.
settingsAdvice.evidence.cpu7b: Planned example: {0} on CPU. Ollama publishes about 4.7 GB file size (decimal GB), not a RAM requirement. This is an estimate from the source, not a locally measured model.
settingsAdvice.evidence.gpu35b: Planned example: {0} on one GPU. OpenHands specifies at least 24 GB VRAM for quantized variants; other variants and multi-GPU setups need separate assessment. No model was downloaded.
settingsAdvice.hardwareSummary: RAM available now: {0} · total GPU VRAM: {1}
settingsAdvice.measuring: Reading computer resources in the background…
settingsAdvice.notMeasured: Computer resources have not been read yet.
settingsAdvice.measurementScope: A lightweight snapshot is taken when AI agents opens and reused for two minutes. VRAM describes each GPU separately and does not establish model server GPU support. Other backends, WSL and containers may have different limits.
settingsAdvice.exact: Have a local Ollama model? Assess it
settingsAdvice.exactHint: Works before the agent is installed. Enter the actual installed model and confirm its server. This check only reads model metadata; it does not select a model for the agent.
